label: r3c1
name: r1c2 with lr 2e-3
hypothesis: Same network and recipe as r1c2, but with learning rate 2e-3 instead of 1e-3. r1c2's training curve was still rising at the end (0.85 to 0.88). Because the rate decays linearly to 0, the last part of training makes small steps, and doubling the rate should finish the job at the same budget. Refuted if dev success is not above 0.913 by more than about 0.03, or if a seed falls into the DONE trap.
last_analysis: Placing logits at the cell each action actually fills (the mirrored head) is what made learning possible. It took dev success from 0 to 0.75–0.94. The best recipe so far uses 128 envs and 3 epochs. A 64-env recipe with 1 or 2 epochs made seeds fall into the trap of choosing DONE first: r2c2 lost both seeds, r2c1 lost one, and r2c3 lost both, so r2c3's architecture result is confounded with that recipe. Raising lr to 2e-3 helped a little: 0.9375 against 0.913, a difference inside the noise, but both seeds were good and the curve was still rising. Adding raw observations to the head did nothing. A separate critic hurt (0.52), so the shared critic seems helpful. The remaining failures are a few cells placed outside the target and stopping too early, which point to how the discount treats the end of the episode and to the lack of global context. This last round tests a higher discount, a higher learning rate, and a cheap global broadcast with the safe recipe.
